title: hidden-reserve-degradation-detection-and-soft-failover-playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
A production escalation from multiple customers (Customer A, Customer B) surfaced intermittent throttles and elevated 429s during burst windows despite metrics indicating available reserved pool headroom. Investigation shows a slow, persistent reserve-count drift caused by two interacting issues: (1) token-lease TTL misalignment between the allocator and autoscaler causing short-lived phantom reservations that are not reclaimed promptly, and (2) KV-cache fragmentation on warm images that increases per-slot memory causing the allocator to overestimate slot utilization. Together these produce 'hidden reserve degradation' where headroom appears healthy on coarse metrics but real assignable capacity is lower, leading to late autoscaler responses and customer-facing throttles.

Impact & Scope:
- Affected tenants: subset of Dedicated tenants using burst credits and high-cardinality small requests (chat-style, 1-2s sessions).
- Customer impact: intermittent 429s and increased latency during peak windows (customer escalations received from two enterprise customers with SLA concerns).
- Frequency: observed spikes 2-3x per week, lasting 5-20 minutes.

Repro Steps / How to Observe:
1) Simulate multi-tenant warmup with many small concurrent sessions (~200-400 concurrent low-QPS clients) against a dedicated pool.
2) Run the allocator with current token-lease TTL (30s) and autoscaler reconcile window (60s).
3) Observe reserved_headroom and assignable_slots metrics; compare to synthetic probe success rate.
4) Note subtle divergence: reserved_headroom remains >= configured threshold while assignable_slots falls.

Root Cause Hypothesis (current):
- Token-lease TTL mismatch: short leases expire and get re-acquired frequently, producing transient allocations that are not visible to the autoscaler's smoothing window, causing the autoscaler to underreact.
- KV-cache fragmentation: warm image snapshots on some GPU types produce uneven memory foot- print per container; allocator counts those as live capacity while real effective slots are fewer.
- Metric aggregation granularity: cluster-level metrics are 30s granularity; the burst admission path needs 1s visibility to prevent micro-throttles.

Immediate Mitigations (done / in-flight):
- Deployed emergency soft-failover routing policy (hotfix): on detection of probe_failure_ratio > 3% for 2 consecutive minutes, route new burst traffic to standby pools (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6129). Status: deployed to prod for three regions, monitoring.
- Increased token-lease TTL from 30s to 90s as a temporary measure to reduce churn (feature flag rollout: allocator.leaseTTL=90). Status: rolled out canary->prod for small AZs.
- Manual reserve replenish runbook executed for affected pools (playbook link below). Status: completed for customers impacted in the last 24h.

Proposed Persistent Fix (roadmap items):
1) Allocator correctness: change allocator accounting to use steady-state slot liveness rather than transient lease counts; implement a 5s smoothing window in allocation pipeline and add reclamation fast-path for orphaned leases. (Owner: Diego Morales)
2) KV-cache introspection: instrument warm image process to emit per-container GPU memory footprint and fragmentation ratio; expose a metric warm_image_fragmentation and gate allocator slot counts on effective_memory_per_slot. (Owner: Lin Wu)
3) Autoscaler visibility: introduce a high-frequency probe metric (1s) and a synthetic tenant probe that runs during burst windows; autoscaler to subscribe to this probe for immediate fallback decisions. (Owner: SRE team)
4) Admission path hardening: add a soft-deny threshold that prefers safe routing over maximizing slot utilization when probe divergence is detected.

Planned Work & Timeline:
- 2026-03-11: Emergency soft-failover deployed and TTL increased (done).
- 2026-03-13: Allocator smoothing prototype merged to staging for soak (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/408).
- 2026-03-17: KV-cache metric instrumentation merged behind flag; begin beta with selected pools.
- 2026-03-20: Autoscaler probe integration and admission policy rollout to prod (target release: runtime-1.20).

Testing & Validation Strategy:
- Create a synthetic workload harness that reproduces the slow degradation over 90+ minutes; include unit tests for lease reclamation and allocation accounting.
- Run canary across AZs with gradual traffic ramp and monitor probe_failure_ratio, assignable_slots, and 429 rates.
- Post-deploy chaos test: simulate rapid lease churn and KV fragmentation to ensure autoscaler fallbacks trigger correctly.

Communications & Customer Follow-up:
- Sent interim incident note to affected customers with mitigations and ETA for fix (Slack/Email).
- Customer success coordination: schedule 1:1 with each impacted customer for 2026-03-15 to review remediation and SLA credits.

Artifacts / Links:
- Playbook / runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/DEDICATED/hidden-reserve-degradation-playbook
- Allocator PR (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/408
- Soft-failover PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6129
- Incident dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/alloc/reserve-degradation

Postmortem Plan:
- Capture full timeline, decisions, and root cause confirmation after persistent fixes are merged and stabilised (owner: Asha Patel). Target PM review and postmortem published by 2026-03-30.

acceptance_criteria: Assignable_slots and reserved_headroom metrics must remain aligned within 2% during synthetic burst workload
Probe_failure_ratio < 0.5% for 7 consecutive days in canary regions
Autoscaler triggers soft-failover within 15s of probe divergence in production
Allocated slot accounting unit tests cover lease churn, orphan reclamation, and per-container memory gating
Customer 429 rates for impacted tenants return to baseline and stay stable for 14 days
